key_takeaways: Indonesia's Marriage Law (Law No. 1 of 1974) makes a marriage legitimate if it is performed according to the laws of the couple's religions and beliefs, and every marriage must be registered.

The Australian Embassy in Indonesia reads this as both partners holding the same religion recognised by the Indonesian Government; confirm what applies to you with the Civil Registry Office or KUA where you would marry.
In January 2023 Indonesia's Constitutional Court dismissed a challenge to that article in full.
The practical alternative: marry legally in Australia, then hold a symbolic ceremony in Bali, which keeps every legal step at home.

faq.q: Is religion required for a civil marriage in Indonesia?
faq.a: The Australian Embassy lists officers of the Civil Registry Office among those who may perform marriages, alongside ministers of religion and the KUA. It also says that, for a marriage to be legal, it must be conducted according to the religion. Confirm the steps with the Civil Registry Office where you would marry.

faq.q: How many witnesses does a legal wedding in Bali need?
faq.a: Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975, which implements the Marriage Law, says the marriage takes place before the Registrar, following the procedure of each religion or belief, and is attended by two witnesses. Your Civil Registry Office confirms the witness rules.

faq.q: Can we marry at the Australian Consulate-General in Bali?
faq.a: No. The Australian Embassy says you cannot marry at the Embassy or a Consulate-General, and you do not register an Indonesian marriage with the Embassy afterwards. For a Bali marriage, the Consulate-General issues the Certificate of No Impediment, usually while you wait if your documents are correct and complete.

faq.q: Can we marry in Bali if one of us is divorced?
faq.a: Not until the divorce is final. The Australian Embassy says you cannot marry before a divorce decree absolute is issued, and its document list for non-Muslim marriages includes proof that a previous marriage was dissolved, or the death certificate of a former partner. Bring originals and photocopies, and check the list with your Civil Registry Office.

faq.q: Can we lodge our Notice of Intended Marriage from overseas?
faq.a: Yes. The Attorney-General's Department says that since 12 June 2024 the notice can be witnessed by audio-visual link, and a couple outside Australia can complete it before an authorised witness overseas, such as an Australian consular officer or a notary public. That overseas witness cannot be a celebrant.
